sources.citation: Delafosse, Maurice. 1929. La langue mandingue et ses dialectes (malinké, bambara, dioula). Vol. I. Paris: Geuthner. §§439-446 'Accentuation', pp.104-105.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online
sources.note: For 'mandingue' as a whole (Malinké/Bambara/Dioula), not Wasulu: 'L'accent tonique, caractérisé en mandingue par la hauteur plus que par l'intensité, et très peu marqué en général, tombe comme en français sur la dernière syllabe du mot' (§441); repeated on the last syllable of each member of compounds (§442); denies lexical tone (§439) — outdated.

sources.citation: Davydov, A.V. 2017. Manden dialekty Gvinei [Manden dialects of Guinea]. In Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande, 164-171 (pp.164-166 on Maninka Wasolon).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Maninka Wasolon = 73,500 speakers (2012 est.), Fulbe who shifted to Manding, Guinean Wasolon dialects close to Manden Maninka; subcontinuum defined by non-inverted tone schemes.

sources.citation: Vydrin, V.F. 2017. Bamana jazyk. In Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande, pp.46-47 (dialect section 1.1.2, 1.2.1).
sources.note: Nothing on stress in the Wasolon passage; states Wasolon and Fuladugu are transitional dialects between Bamana and Maninka and that the Wasolon dialect was monographically described by Salabary Doumbia (1987). Bamana chapter 2.1.2 is a tonal-system section with no stress sentence.

sources.citation: Vydrin, V.F. 2017. Mande jazyki [Mande languages]. In Vydrin, Mazurova, Kibrik & Markus (eds.), Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande, 16-45. SPb: Nestor-Istorija. p.34.
sources.note: Family-level only: 'Ударение в большинстве М.я. отсутствует. Там, где оно может быть выделено (в частности, бамана), его функциональная нагрузка невелика.' (Stress is absent in most Mande languages; where it can be identified, e.g. Bamana, its functional load is small; Bamana foot stress mentioned). Not Wasulu-specific.

sources.citation: Bird, Charles S. (ed.) 1982 [1981]. The Dialects of Mandekan. Bloomington: Indiana University (ERIC ED210934). Wasulu listed among eastern dialects (p.13); general tone section; Wasulu sketch C.2 incl. '4. Tone'.
sources.note: No word-stress statement for Wasulu. Wasulu sketch: 'Tone operates in the same manner as the Bamako system described above.' General tone section: 'In the Bambara dialects, it will often be the case that the last of a series of high tone words receives a stress accent. This accent leads to a tonal readjustment in which the accented syllable is raised and the preceding high tones gradually rise to it' (phrase-level, tonal).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3. Languoid wasu1256 'Wasulu (Retired)' (bookkeeping); wasu1254 'Wasulu' (dialect of Eastern Maninkakan east2426); wasu1257 'Wasulu (Wojenaka)' (dialect of Wojenaka woje1238). https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/wasu1256
sources.note: Nothing; retired entry with no references, and Glottolog lists no references for either successor dialect languoid.
